title: Garden Tool Tap
hook: Care for the bed, then let the garden be.
roundStructure: Round 1 lexical-semantic A-Z; Round 2 retrieval-action A-Z; 4+4+4+4+4+4+2 chunks
responseSpace: one beat with woodblock muted after cue
visualStyle: clean 3D garden-tool storybook, bright shed colors, simple soil-and-leaf backdrop, safe friendly tools, strong separation

creativeFingerprint.pointOfView: a child observing and helping only with safe garden-care motions while adults handle tools that require distance
creativeFingerprint.chorusFunction: reset the care sequence—touch the rhythm, then leave space for growth rather than celebrating tools themselves
creativeFingerprint.grooveMeter: stop-go 4/4 care rhythm with muted tap-rest figures
creativeFingerprint.round1Grammar: hand-written care sequence; practical verbs describe compost, mulch, containers, watering and safe tools, while flowers/food show the living result rather than being treated as equipment
creativeFingerprint.round2Grammar: care cue -> recall beat -> target -> safe mime/point/shape action; adult-only tools remain observation-only
creativeFingerprint.sectionContrast: Verses stay sparse; chorus widens; retrieval strips back. marimba seed-to-sprout answer figures and tiny shaker breaths
creativeFingerprint.signatureColor: marimba seed-to-sprout answer figures and tiny shaker breaths
creativeFingerprint.authorialIntent: Make garden care feel like a sequence of small purposeful actions: prepare, feed, protect, water, wait and notice what the work makes possible.
creativeFingerprint.lyricIdentity: A child watches safe garden work from close range; tap, pat, scrape, spread, pour and pause form a restrained work rhythm while plants show the result of care.
semanticArc: notice plants and materials already there
finish by watering, waiting and seeing what the bed can support
